This intra-court appeal is preferred against the order dated 13th December 2021 passed in Writ petition number 26054 of 2015 by the learned single judge.
2. Brief facts of the case leading to filing of this appeal are that the appellant/Karnataka Police Employees House Building Co-operative Society (for short hereinafter referred to as "Society"),

sentences.text: registered
under the provisions of Co-operative Societies Act, 1959,

with an object of providing housing sites to its members, represented to the Government on 6th March 2006, requesting it to convey land in survey number 54, measuring 1 acre, 32 guntas; in survey number 68/1 Measuring 6 acre 7 guntas, which came within the precincts of Mysore Urban Development Authority for short hereinafter after referred to as "MUDA").
The said land was acquired by MUDA by issuance of preliminary notification dated 15th July 1997, followed by final notification on 18th January 2002.
MUDA also had taken possession of the land after issuance of final notification.
The Society sought the land for the purpose of allotting sites to its members.
There were correspondences between Government and MUDA upon the request made by the Society.
On 17th January 2007, MUDA also communicated to the Government that the land which the Society sought, was convenient for formation of a residential layout.

Based on the communication of MUDA dated 17th January 2007,
the acquired land had to be delivered in favour of the Society after collecting entire award amount that was paid to the land owners by MUDA.

In turn, MUDA on 19th September 2007, informed the Society that in terms of the government's communication the land would be handed over to the Society and the Society was also directed to pay the amount of Rs.30,02,760/-, which was the compensation that the MUDA had paid to the land-owners in the year 1997.
Pursuant to the said demand, MUDA passed an order directing, handing over of possession of the aforesaid land to the Society acknowledging receipt of the amount demanded.
On 7th November 2007, the Society was handed over with physical possession of the land along with sketch of the land.
After all the necessities came about, MUDA also executed a registered sale deed in favour of the Society on 1st March 2008.

On transfer of the land to the Society, the land owners in survey number 68/1 measuring 6 acre 7 guntas, filed Writ Petitions No.1393-1397 of 2009 before this Court seeking to Karnataka Police Employees House ... vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192523722/
2 set aside the order dated 17th July 2007, which was Government's communication to MUDA to transfer the land to the Society.

sentences.text:
This court, by order dated 02nd September, 2010, dismissed the writ petitions with liberty to the petitioners therein to approach MUDA for any other benefit,
including the benefit of allotment of sites.
The finding in the writ petition became final as the land owners had not challenged the same any further.

Between 14th September 2009, and 20th December 2011, the Deputy commissioner, Mysuru, on an application being made by the Society,
passed an order permitting conversion of the land from agriculture to non- agricultural purposes and the revenue entries and other municipal entries were made in favour of the Society.
Further, it is stated that after the approvals and conversion, a layout plan was also submitted by the Society which was approved by MUDA.
In terms of the approval of a plan, layout was formed and sites were allotted to the members of the Society.

On 28th June 2013, MUDA also released all the sites in favour of the Society and on several dates in the year 2013-14, the Society executed registered sale deeds in respect of the members of the Society.
The sites were registered at the rate of Rs.208.35 paise per square feet, including development costs incurred for the formation of layout.

Therefore,
formation of layout, allotment of sites, registration of sale deed in favour of the members of the Society, were all over by the year 2014.

It is further stated that as things stood thus, MUDA issued notice to the Society demanding Rs.3,37,74,476/- on the ground that the land-losers had approached the Reference Court seeking enhancement of compensation and the Reference court enhanced the compensation pursuant to which warrant was issued in the Execution Petition and the MUDA had deposited entire amount determined by the Reference Court which was sought to be executed.

The Society replied to MUDA seeking all documents, to furnish a suitable reply and there being no response from the hands of MUDA, the Society knocked the doors of this Court challenging the notice dated 7th March 2015, which demanded the aforesaid amount.
The said Writ Petition was dismissed by order dated 13th December 2021 by the learned Single Judge.
Being aggrieved by the dismissal of the writ petition, the Society has preferred this appeal.

3. Sri K.R. Krishnamurthy, learned Counsel appearing for the appellant submits that the Government informed to MUDA to handover the land for formation of layout by the Society clearly indicating that whatever compensation has been paid by MUDA shall be recovered from the Society.
As on that date Rs.30,02,760/- was the compensation that was paid to the land owners and the Society had paid the same to MUDA.
Sale deeds were executed in favour of the Society, noticing the consideration and no other claim.
Therefore, it forms a concluded contract between the MUDA and the Society.
Now MUDA or the Government had indicated that the petitioner appellant herein, will have to bear the compensation in the event the same is enhanced.
Plea of estoppel against MUDA is put forth by the Society and sought quashing of notice dated 7th March 2015.

The transaction between the Society and MUDA is a sale transaction at the market value which is mutually agreed upon and there is no acquisition in favour of the Society and the appellant-Society is not the beneficiary of the acquisition.

The Government has taken decision to transfer the land under the circumstance that the land is falling in the middle of the layout approved by the MUDA in favour of the appellant-Society and the same is not suitable for MUDA to form the layout.
That apart, the Society is also allotting the sites to its members and thereby purpose of utilisation of land is not defeated.

Karnataka Police Employees House ... vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192523722/

sentences.text: Learned Counsel would further submit that the notice issued by the MUDA is liable to be quashed as the same is wholly illegal and arbitrary.

The conclusion of the learned single judge that the sale deed is not a concluded contract between MUDA and Society is perverse and illegal having regard to the express discharge given by the MUDA to the Society from making any further payment.
The appellant- Society is not the beneficiary of the acquisition proceedings.
The Society has only sought for transfer of the land to it with an offer to pay an amount at Rs.2,50,000/- per acre as and by way of consideration.

Such an offer was made in the circumstance that the said lands were situated in the layout to be formed by the Society, and though the same was acquired by the MUDA, the lands were not suitable for formation of layout by the MUDA having regard to its location.
The offer was accepted by the Government and the MUDA.
There was no counter offer made nor additional condition imposed either by the Government or by MUDA.
That the transaction is a transaction between the MUDA and the Society, and as such, the Society is not liable to pay any amount exceeding the amount reflected in the Sale deed.
It is further submitted that the learned single judge ought to have considered the application on principles of "accord and satisfaction".

The learned Single Judge grossly erred in concluding that the absence of clause in the sale deed dated 29th February 2008, would not enure to the benefit of the Society to contend that it is a concluded contract, is illegal and perverse.
MUDA is trying to put the Society into predicament situation after committing serious negligence in contesting the proceeding for enhancement.
The Reference Court has enhanced the compensation to Rs.10,61,000/- per acre, and the same was challenged by MUDA contending that the enhancement do not represent the true market value.
The Reference Court found that such a fixation of market value by the Reference Court is without following the guidelines issued by the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
The matter was remitted back to the Reference Court.
After remand, the Reference Court has enhanced the compensation.
The order of Reference Court was accepted by the land owners and as such there is no occasion for the land owners to seek for further enhancement.
MUDA, after the remand, did not even contest the matter.

After suffering the order,
to cover-up its negligence, the MUDA, instead of challenging the enhancement, sought to recover the amount from the Society, which is inequitable and unjust.
The learned judge failed to appreciate that the demand made by the MUDA is barred by time.

The MUDA, knowing fully well that the application for enhancement of compensation was pending before the Reference Court,
acknowledged the payment received from the Society and further discharged the appellant from making any further payments vide recitals in the sale deed dated 29th February 2008.
Hence, the demand notice dated 7th March 2015 is barred by time.

He further contended that the observation of the learned Single Judge that the Society could have impleaded itself into the reference proceedings do not stand to any reason for the fact that the Society is not the beneficiary of acquisition proceedings, and having knowledge of the pendency of enhancement proceedings had given complete discharge to the Society from making any further payment in the recital of the sale deed.

Further, the observation of the learned single judge that the Society and its members are beneficiaries of formation of layout and holding the property are bound to comply with the payment of enhanced compensation, is illogical and perverse as the Society is not the beneficiary and the acquisition of land is by the MUDA.

Society has already registered the sites in favour of its members at the rate of Rs.208.35 paise per square feet - 10 - Karnataka Police Employees House ... vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192523722/
4 which includes development costs incurred for formation of the layout.

sentences.text: Having regard to the confirmation by the MUDA in the sale deed dated 29th February 2008, the Society is acquitted and discharged from making any further payment and the Society did not reserve any right to collect the amounts in respect of the site in the sale deeds executed in favour of its members and the Society has no resource to pay additional amounts and also is not in a position to collect money from the members to whom sites are allotted.
On all these grounds, the learned council sort to allow the appeal.

In support of his submission, he relied on the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED v. BOGHARA POLYFAB PRIVATE LIMITED reported in (2009)1 SCC 267.
5.

sentences.text: On the other hand, the learned Counsel Sri T.P. Vivekananda, appearing for the respondent-MUDA, would support the order passed by the learned Single Judge and further would submit that the MUDA being a government institution under the Urban Development Authority, has handed over the land at the request of the Society by the Government under Section 65 of the Urban Development Authority Act.
The land owners have challenged acquisition proceedings in Writ - 11 - Petitions No.1393-1397 of 2009 and the same was dismissed by order dated 2nd November 2010.
The Society was aware of the fact that the land owners have filed petition seeking enhancement of compensation.
Knowing fully well, MUDA has requested the government for allotting the land to the Society.

A perusal of the communication from the Society to the urban Development Department,
clearly indicates that MUDA was not completely in favour of handing over the land to the Society and the Society made representation to the Government to consider its claim sympathetically contended that it would also be bound to pay the compensation which was paid to the land- losers.
The objection of MUDA was notified in communication dated 9th February 2007 and 17th January 2007.
The Society has undertook to pay the compensation to the land-losers.
The Society is the beneficiary of the land and hence it is liable to pay the amount which was demanded by the MUDA which is already paid as per order of the Court.

The MUDA or the Government are not liable to pay compensation to the land- losers as the land was handed over to the Society only upon the request made by the Society and it has agreed to pay the compensation.
On all these grounds, it was sought for dismissal of the appeal.
We have given our anxious consideration to the contentions, advanced by the learned Council appearing for the parties.
7. We have examined the material placed before this Court.

A perusal of the same makes it clear that the Society submitted representation to the Hon'ble Chief Minister on 6th March 2006 in which it is sought for allotment of land in survey numbers 54, 68/1, and 218 of Lalitadri village Varuna Hubli Mysore Taluk.
The total extent of 12 acre 01 gunta to the Society to form residential layout.
Pursuant to the said representation.

A note was generated by the office of Hon'ble Chief Minister for examination of records and handing over of land in an extent of 12 acre 01 gunta in survey numbers Karnataka Police Employees House ... vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192523722/
5 54, 68/1, and 218 of Lalitadri village, Varuna Hobli, Mysore Taluk, to the Society.

sentences.text: In furtherance of the documents, a communication was issued to the Secretary, Urban Development Department for release of land in the above stated survey numbers in favour of the Society.
The correspondence between MUDA and the Government took place as per to the request of the Society.

The communication between Society and MUDA resulted in the Society accepting the conditions that would be incorporated with regard to the - 13 - compensation that is to be paid for handing over of the land as was sought for.
The communication made by the Society to the Urban Development Department would clearly indicate that MUDA was not completely in favour of handing over the land to the Society.

It is noticed that the Society requested the Government to consider its claim sympathetically, and it would also be bound to pay the compensation that was granted to the land losers which is forthcoming in the objection of MUDA.
All these materials makes it clear that the Society becomes the beneficiary of the land acquired by the MUDA.
MUDA has only acted as per directions of the government in transferring the land in question to the Society.

8. It is an undisputed fact that the land owners who had lost their lands pursuant to acquisition in the year 2002, filed Writ Petitions No.1393-1397 of 2009, the moment sale deed were executed in favour of the Society, contending that The land was acquired for the benefit of MUDA and is now transferred to the benefit of the Society.
Therefore, it is illegal and at the same breath, the land owners had filed petition before the Reference Court.
This Court, dismissed the writ petitions with liberty to the petitioners therein to approach the respondents seeking benefit of allotment of sites.

Thereafter,
- 14 - the land was converted for residential purpose by order of the Deputy Commissioner and sites were formed and distributed to the members of the Society.
9. The Reference Court enhanced the amount of compensation to be paid to the lands acquired.
The amount determined by the Reference Court was sought to be executed and accordingly warrant of execution was issued against MUDA by the Executing Court.
The letter addressed by the Secretary of the Society indicates that MUDA was not completely in favour of handing over the land to the Society.
It is noticed that the Society requested the Government to consider its claim and the Society would also be bound by the compensation that was granted to the land losers.
One the objection of MUDA, which was noticed in the communication dated 9th February 2007 is not disputed by the Society.
When the Society has undertook to pay the compensation amount to the MUDA, that compensation amount cannot be restricted only to the compensation determined by the Special Land Acquisition Officer.

The word 'compensation' include all statutory benefits like solatium,
additional market value and interest, as required under Sections 23(2), 23(1-A) and 28 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, as decided by the Full Bench of Karnataka Police Employees House ... vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192523722/

sentences.text: The compensation amount cannot be restricted only to the extent of compensation awarded by the Special Land Acquisition Officer.
The compensation has not attained finality.

In the case on hand,
the fact that the Reference Court has enhanced the compensation is within the knowledge of the appellant-Society.
Fortunately, the land-losers have not preferred any appeal against the compensation awarded by the Reference Court.

Therefore, the award passed by the Reference Court attains finality and the Society is bound to pay the said amount to the MUDA as undertaken by it as per letter addressed to the Hon'ble Chief Minister as well as to MUDA.
The appellant- Society has not placed any material to show that it is liable only to pay the amount of compensation awarded by the Tribunal only to the extent of Rs.30,02,760/-.
Therefore, MUDA has got every right to take steps to recover the said amount from the appellant-Society.
In view of the discussions made above, we cannot accept the arguments advanced on behalf of the appellant-Society.

10. Learned Counsel for the appellant submitted that MUDA has not properly contested the case before the Reference - 16 - Court and is trying to put the Society in the predicament situation after committing serious negligence in contesting the proceeding for enhancement.

In this regard, a perusal of the material placed before this Court makes it clear that Reference Court has enhanced the compensation to Rs.10,61,000/- per acre and same was challenged by the MUDA contending that the enhancement do not represent the true market value and such a fixation of market value by the Reference Court is without following guidelines issued by the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
The matter was remitted back to the Reference Court.
After remand, the Reference Court enhanced the compensation.
The land-owners have not preferred appeal against the said award passed by the Reference Court.
Under the given set of circumstances, we find no material to show that MUDA has not taken proper legal steps to contest the proceedings before the Reference Court.
Hence the arguments advanced by the Society that MUDA has not contested the case properly, cannot be accepted.
11. Further, the learned counsel for the appellant would submit that the learned Single Judge failed to appreciate that the demand made by MUDA is barred by time.

The learned Counsel would submit that MUDA is estopped from issuing - 17 - demand notice to the Society as it has executed a sale deed in favour of the Society by receiving consideration amount, and the Society has satisfied the complete consideration amount shown in the sale deed.
Hence, in view of the principle of "accord and satisfaction", the authority has no right to issue the demand notice to the appellant-Society.
The said plea is taken for the first time in this appeal and the same was not urged or canvassed before the learned Single Judge.
Hence, the same cannot be accepted.

In that view of the matter the reliance placed by the learned Counsel for the Karnataka Police Employees House ... vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192523722/
7

sentences.text: Society in the case of BOGHARA POLYFAB PRIVATE LIMITED will not enure to the benefit of the Society.
Be that as it may, the MUDA has not allotted the land to the appellant Society on its own volition.

On the contrary, at the request made by the Society to the Hon'ble Chief Minister, the state government has considered the request and directed the MUDA and then only the MUDA has complied with the order of the State Government and handed over the land to the Society.

The Society, being beneficiary of the acquired land, will have to pay not only the compensation that was awarded by the Special Land Acquisition Officer, but also the enhanced compensation awarded by the Reference Court to the land-losers.
Hence, the principle of "accord and satisfaction" is not applicable to the case on hand.

On consideration/examination of the entire material placed before us, we do not find any error/legal infirmities in the order dated 13th December, 2021 passed by the learned Single Judge in Writ Petition No.26054 of 2015.
Resultantly, appeal is dismissed.
